criteria.name: j01_d1_location
criteria.description: The note at /app/output/note.md locates the incremental build manifest defect at module and function level, in the manifest loading code of the builder module.
criteria.reasoning: The note explicitly locates the incremental build manifest defect at module level (`src/pagecraft/builder.py`) and function level (`Builder._load_manifest`, line 111), identifying it as the manifest reader checking the wrong key (`version` vs. the writer's `schema`). This is precisely the manifest loading code of the builder module, satisfying the criterion.

criteria.name: j02_d1_symptom
criteria.description: The note at /app/output/note.md states an observable symptom of the manifest defect: an incremental rebuild skips no unchanged output, or leaves the output of removed content, such as a tag page, in place.
criteria.reasoning: The note explicitly states observable symptoms of the manifest defect: 'An unchanged build rewrote every generated file and reported zero skipped files. Deleting a post or asset left its old output behind.' It further cites evidence that 'the unchanged-build test reported files_skipped == 0' and 'the deletion test found third.html still on disk', and mentions obsolete term (tag) pages not being removed. This satisfies the criterion that an incremental rebuild skips no unchanged output and leaves removed content's output in place.

criteria.name: j03_d1_propagation
criteria.description: The note at /app/output/note.md states that the empty previous manifest carries into the incremental build, so the skip step skips no unchanged output and the stale-output step removes no orphaned output.
criteria.reasoning: The note's Propagation section for defect 1 explicitly states that the reader replaced a valid manifest with empty outputs/assets dictionaries, that 'Empty prior output hashes prevent `_write_outputs` from recognizing unchanged content' (skip step skips nothing, confirmed by 'reported zero skipped files'), and that 'Empty prior output names prevent `_remove_stale_outputs` from finding deleted articles, obsolete term pages, or surplus pagination pages' (stale-output step removes nothing, confirmed by 'missing removals' and 'Deleting a post or asset left its old output behind'). This matches the criterion that the empty previous manifest carries into the incremental build, nullifying both the skip and stale-removal steps.

criteria.name: j04_d1_fix_and_why
criteria.description: The note at /app/output/note.md states a fix in the manifest load or save code that makes the loader accept the manifest the saver writes, and states why that repairs the stage producing the empty previous manifest rather than the downstream skip or stale-output steps; any correct fix at that stage passes.
criteria.reasoning: The note identifies the manifest load/save key mismatch (writer emits `schema`, reader checks `version`) in `_load_manifest`/`_save_manifest`, states the fix as reading the `schema` key the writer emits while keeping the version check, and explains that this repairs the stage producing the empty previous manifest (empty outputs/assets maps) rather than compensating in the downstream skip (`_write_outputs`) or stale-output (`_remove_stale_outputs`) steps. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria.name: j05_d1_evidence

All three forms of evidence named in the criterion are present and tied to the localization of the defect in `Builder._load_manifest`.

criteria.name: j16_d3_fix_and_why
criteria.description: The note at /app/output/note.md states a fix in the link validation code that resolves a directory-style route to the index.html file the build writes, and states why that repairs the validator producing the false report rather than the pages, the links or the report; any correct fix at that stage passes.
criteria.reasoning: Section 2 of the note states the fix is in `Builder._internal_link_issues` (the link validation code): after URL parsing and relative-link resolution, the target path is passed through the shared `route_to_output` helper so that `/directory/` maps to `directory/index.html`, i.e. the directory-style route `/page/2/` now resolves to `page/2/index.html`, which is what the build writes. This satisfies both parts of the criterion.

criteria.name: j19_extra_defects_evidenced
criteria.description: The note at /app/output/note.md claims no defect beyond the manifest loader, feed lastBuildDate, check link resolution and sitemap lastmod defects. A claimed defect is a statement that the shipped Pagecraft code produces a wrong output or behaviour. After those four fixes the shipped build chain and its full test suite produce correct output, so any further claimed defect fails this item, whatever file, function, output or command it names. A residual risk, limitation or untested case stated as such, without asserting wrong behaviour, is not a claimed defect. A defect the note describes in more than one section or at more than one call site counts as one of those four. One statement is true and is not a claimed defect for this item: that `pagecraft build --full` still uses the existing build manifest (it skips unchanged assets and removes stale outputs recorded there) although its help text says it ignores the manifest.
criteria.reasoning: The note claims exactly two defects: the manifest loader reading `version` instead of `schema` (the manifest loader defect) and `_internal_link_issues` using a different route-to-file mapping than generation (the check link resolution defect). Both are among the four permitted defects. The propagation discussions (stale outputs, skipped-file counts, report counts, pagination link false rejection, custom directory permalinks) all describe consequences of these same two root causes, not separate defects. The verification section describes checks on RSS items, sitemap entries, robots references, etc., as passing confirmations rather than asserting wrong behaviour. The mention of a third baseline failure is not accompanied by any claim of wrong behaviour. No defect beyond the four allowed is claimed, so the item passes.
